assertion_analysis.self_referential: No newly added assertion is unconditionally true regardless of the code under test; propagation/identity assertions at 303,432,493 are limited to linkage and are not counted alone as classification, fsync or recovery coverage.
assertion_analysis.tests/test_session_scratch_uses_bounded_: Removing the configured two-hour grace, changing its default, or losing it during host override makes the full expected dictionaries fail; expectations are independent product requirements, not echoed arguments.
Restoring a single post-removal row, omitting an intent/completion, double counting bytes or duplicating records on a second pass fails known fixture-size totals, the literal state sequence or literal row count.

The holder readiness assertion fails if the real subprocess does not start; the return-code assertion fails if disk sampling refuses publication; these are setup/integration checks rather than classification evidence.

Removing live-child inspection, including held/recent entries, assigning the wrong owner, using zero/allocated bytes instead of the known sparse logical size, or computing the wrong age fails the fixture-derived count, path, size, age and identities.

Dropping pressure propagation or owner/path/byte/age text fails the returned list equality and literal required substrings; line 303 is an input-to-output propagation check only and supplies no independent evidence that classification is correct, which is supplied by lines 294-301.
Deleting the live tree or either protected sibling fails physical size/content checks and empty removal/audit expectations; changing the CLI field contract fails the four-token assertion.

Bypassing sink opening or error reporting fails setup/error assertions; reinstating delete-before-record makes the independently saved physical tree and payload assertions fail for write, flush and fsync refusal.
Restoring a shared expired deadline or restarting sorted traversal every pass retains the small tree and loses its removal result; removing the unreadable slow tree also fails physical survival.

Reusing the initial deadline for the final walk makes the controlled four-second walks fail removal and the strict later-deadline comparison; this compares deadlines generated by the code against independently advanced time, not a supplied expected deadline.

Restoring deletion before intent persistence fails assertions executed at the real rmtree boundary: intent state, known path/size/age/reason, observed fsync of the log and one pending receipt with matching identity; the identity comparison proves linkage, not durability by itself.
Failure to remove, wrong intent/completion ordering, or leaving a completed pending receipt fails the removal result, literal journal states or physical pending-directory enumeration.

Swallowing the injected second-write error, deleting too late, removing the pending intent early or persisting wrong metadata fails the error, physical absence, pending count and literal/fixture-derived intent fields.

Omitting reconciliation, reporting an absent path as retained, linking a different operation or failing to retire the receipt fails count, completion state, original durable identity and physical receipt absence.

Removing the post-publication pointer check deletes the tree and changes the empty removal list and intent/retained journal states; these assertions do not cover descendant writes that leave no pointer or descriptor.

findings.text: blocking: the final descendant activity walk occurs before record_removal(state=intent), which can block on several writes/fsyncs; the subsequent refusal checks only the root ctime, live pointer and current holders, so an existing descendant written and closed during publication leaves the root ctime unchanged and is deleted at line 1765 despite being touched inside the grace period; repeat the fail-closed descendant activity check after intent acknowledgement and add a control that refreshes an existing payload during publication without creating a pointer or leaving an open descriptor.
